before: The shipped `arcridge.sundial` 0.4.2 board knows only whether the current workspace is linked and whether its folder name starts with a spec ID.
It disables worktree creation in every linked worktree, cannot identify an associated worktree elsewhere, and opens worktrees with Sundial-owned Git and `vscode.openFolder` logic.
Navigation uses VS Code's stable `vscode.openFolder` command with a file URI and current-window reuse.
after: Spawned worktrees are trusted by default without disabling VS Code Workspace Trust. VS Code's stable extension API can observe trust but cannot grant it to an arbitrary URI, so new worktrees live under the already-trusted main repository at `.sundial-worktrees/<spec-file-basename>`. VS Code then inherits the main folder's trust. The editor CLI idempotently adds `.sundial-worktrees/` to the common repository's `.git/info/exclude` so the local container does not dirty the main checkout or require a tracked ignore rule. Existing worktrees outside that trusted parent retain VS Code's normal trust behavior.
